name: Didone
summary: The extreme of the roman: a vertical stress, hairline serifs with no bracket, and a strong contrast between stem and hairline. At display sizes it is the voice of fashion and luxury; in small text it sparkles and tires the eye.

philosophy.core_thesis: A letter is a geometric figure of thick and thin, cut as fine as the metal and the paper allow.
design_principles: Keep the stroke contrast at 4:1 or more in text cuts and 8:1 or more in display cuts, measured on the o.
Set the stress exactly vertical: the thinnest parts of the o are at 12 and 6 o'clock.
Draw the serifs as flat hairlines with no bracket, at a right angle to the stem.
Use ball terminals on a, c, f, g, j, r and y.
Set the face at 18 pt or more; at text sizes, use an optical cut with heavier hairlines.
Give the page wide white space; the face needs air around it.
anti_patterns: Text below 10 pt in a display cut with 10:1 contrast
Low-resolution or low-contrast backgrounds that break the hairlines
Wide positive tracking on the lower case
Heavy, rounded corners on the stems

classification.note: A Didone has hairline serifs with no bracket; a face that keeps a bracket is Transitional. The British Standard calls the class Modern.

anatomy.contrast: Extreme: the hairlines are 0.05–0.25 of the stem.
anatomy.serifs: Flat hairline serifs with no bracket, or a very small one.
anatomy.terminals: Round ball terminals on a, c, f, g, j, r and y.
anatomy.aperture: Closed: the c, e and s curl in on themselves.
anatomy.key_letters: A narrow-bowled a with a ball, an R with a straight or curled leg, and capitals with even widths.

metrics.x_height: The x-height is 0.58–0.74 of the cap height; display revivals sit at the top of the range.
metrics.contrast: The side of the o is 4 to 14 times as thick as its top; display cuts go past 10:1.
metrics.width: Capitals tend to an even width; the lower case is of medium width, 0.48–0.55 em mean advance.
metrics.figures: Lining figures with ball terminals on 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 9.

setting.text_sizes: Use a text cut (optical size 6–12) at 11–14 pt in print or 18–22 px on screen, and only for short text.
setting.display_sizes: Use the display cut at 24–200 pt for titles, mastheads and covers.
setting.leading: Set the leading at 1.0–1.1 times the size for titles and 1.4–1.6 for text.
setting.tracking: Set titles at −0.02 to 0 em; letter-space capitals by 0.06–0.15 em.
setting.measure: Set 45–60 characters a line for text; titles are short lines of 1–4 words.
setting.case_and_features: Use capitals with generous tracking for mastheads, and the italic for subtitles.

pairing.rule: Use the Didone for display only and pair it with a quiet text face of low contrast.

pairs.role: sans for text, captions and navigation
pairs.why: Both are constructed faces, and the even sans gives rest after the high contrast of the titles.
It keeps the vertical stress but holds the hairlines at text sizes.

reference_faces.note: Bodoni Moda has optical sizes: its default instance (opsz 11) is a text cut with about 5:1 contrast. Playfair Display mixes Didone contrast with a large, transitional x-height.

evidence.title: Manuale tipografico (1818), a page of capitals
evidence.credit: Published by his widow, Parma; scan on Wikimedia Commons

emotion.target_response: Glamour and poise: the reader feels luxury, fashion and a cool distance.

avoid_when: The text is long and set below 11 pt or 16 px.
The output prints on rough paper or shows on a low-resolution screen.
The brief asks for an informal or friendly voice.

modifiers.how: Add brackets to the serifs, bring the contrast down to 3–4:1, and open the apertures.
Make the hairlines heavy and the serifs square, as in the fat faces and Egyptians that came next.

x_height_ratio.note: Playfair Display sits at the top; Bodoni and Didot sit near 0.40.

tracking.note: The top of the range is for letter-spaced capitals.

sources.title: Robert Bringhurst, The Elements of Typographic Style (Hartley & Marks, 4th ed. 2012)
